title: Dipper discs not inclined towards edge-on orbits
question: Are dipper stars' disks all viewed nearly edge-on, as assumed by the proposed dip mechanisms?

what.value: Inclination of EPIC 204638512, 6±1.5 deg, from 12CO first-moment map

evidence.quote: we adopt the disk inclination of $i=6$$^\circ$$\pm$1.5$^\circ$ derived by (cite: 2012ApJ...753...59M)

what.value: Stellar properties (SpT, Teff, AV, disk type)

evidence.quote: Stellar properties are from the literature (cite: 2002A&A...393..597N; 2014ApJ...787...42C; 2016ApJ...816...69A).

recipe.method: uvmodelfit elliptical Gaussian to visibilities; inclination from aspect ratio assuming circular disk; checked against CO first-moment map
assumptions: circular disk structure, Keplerian rotation for moment-map check

recipe.method: uvmodelfit elliptical Gaussian with initial PA≈20 deg, then imfit image-plane check

evidence.quote: we found a nearly edge-on disk with $i=73$$^\circ$$\pm$23$^\circ$, $F=4.2\pm0.1$ mJy

not_stated_but_needed: Which ALMA calibrated products/images were used for EPIC 204638512 and 205151387 and their processing
Image size, cell size, clean threshold for the images
uvmodelfit initial guesses and region/fit settings for EPIC 205151387
